title: Moving & Roommates
description: The real cost of a move, a fair split, and a plan for the day someone leaves.
wolfLine: Write the split down before you share a fridge.

roommate-agreement.definition: A written note of who pays what, who gets which room, and what happens if someone leaves. It sits next to the lease. It does not replace it.
roommate-agreement.example: Rent is $1,800. The larger room pays $1,200. The smaller room pays $600. Electric and internet are split in half.

lessons.title: What Moving Costs
lessons.summary: The truck is the small line.

steps.title: Add the lines
steps.body: People remember the truck and forget the deposit. On this move the truck is **$180**. The first month and the [[security deposit]] are **$1,600** each.

steps.prompt: What is the cash to move on this page?
How much of that $3,510 is the first month plus the deposit?
How much is the truck, the boxes, and the utility start, added together?
The security deposit on this page is a cost you have spent forever.
steps.explain: It is held. If you leave the place undamaged and paid up, it should come back.

lessons.title: Split by Room Size
lessons.summary: The bigger room pays the bigger share.

steps.title: Use the square feet
steps.body:
The rent is **$1,800**. One room is **400** square feet. The other is **200**. Together that is **600**.

The larger room is 400 ÷ 600 of the rent. The smaller is 200 ÷ 600.

steps.prompt: What does the 400-square-foot room pay out of $1,800?
What does the 200-square-foot room pay out of $1,800?
Do those two shares add back to the full rent?
Splitting every rent bill in half is fair when one room is twice the other.
steps.explain: Half and half ignores the size. Here the fair split is $1,200 and $600.

lessons.title: Shared Bills
lessons.summary: Write the split down while you still like each other.

steps.title: Rent is not the only bill
steps.body:
Electric is **$90**. Internet is **$60**. Together that is **$150**.

A [[roommate agreement]] says who pays which share, and when. The [[lease]] still makes each signer responsible to the landlord.

steps.prompt: Electric is $90 and internet is $60. What is the shared-bill total?
Two roommates split that $150 in half. What does each pay?
If they split the $150 the way they split the rooms, 2/3 and 1/3, what does the larger room pay?
The landlord was not in the room when you agreed. Who can the landlord still ask for the full rent?
choices: Only the roommate who took the bigger room
Nobody, once you have a roommate agreement
steps.explain: The agreement splits the bill between you. The lease is what the landlord enforces.

lessons.title: If Someone Leaves
lessons.summary: The landlord does not take a smaller check.

steps.title: The empty room is still on the lease
steps.body:
Rent is **$1,800**, split **$900** and **$900**. One roommate moves out. The lease still says **$1,800** until a new roommate is approved and added.

You can chase your former roommate for their share. The landlord can chase you for the whole rent.

steps.prompt: You were paying $900 of an $1,800 rent. Your roommate leaves. What does the landlord still expect this month?
steps.explain: The lease amount does not shrink. It is still $1,800.

steps.prompt: How much more is that than the $900 you had been paying?
What belongs in the roommate agreement for this moment?
choices: Who pays until a new roommate is approved, and how you find one
A note that the landlord will cut the rent in half
steps.explain: Write the plan before anyone is angry.

steps.prompt: A roommate agreement lets you pay only your old share after the other person moves out.
steps.explain: It can say your roommate still owes you. It cannot force the landlord to accept half the rent.

lessons.title: Utilities
lessons.summary: Start the new ones before you end the old ones.

steps.title: A week in the dark is expensive
steps.body:
The start-up charge on this account is **$60**. A typical electric bill after that is **$90**.

Turn the new place on before move-in day. Turn the old place off the day you return the keys, not a month later.

steps.prompt: The first month is the $60 start-up plus a $90 electric bill. What is that first utility month?
After the start-up, you budget $90 a month. What is electric for a 12-month lease, counting the start-up once?
You leave the old electric on for an extra month at $90. What did that month buy?
choices: Power for an apartment you no longer use
A discount at the new place
steps.explain: Schedule the stop date. An empty apartment still bills you.

steps.prompt: The internet account can stay in a roommate’s name after they move out, with no risk to them.
steps.explain: The name on the account is the person the company will bill. Put the account with someone who still lives there.

lessons.title: Two Apartments
lessons.summary: Compare the month, not the rent line.

steps.prompt: What is Apartment A per month, rent plus utilities?
What is Apartment B per month, rent plus the internet you still pay?
How much less is A than B, once both pages are included?
You care only about the monthly cash. Which page wins?
why: B’s rent looks higher because heat and water are inside it, and the total is still higher.
steps.explain: A is $1,680. B is $1,810. A is $130 less.

steps.prompt: The lower rent line is always the cheaper apartment.
steps.explain: B’s rent is higher and its full month is higher here. On another pair, a higher rent can still be cheaper once utilities are added.

lessons.title: Ben and Ola
lessons.summary: The rooms are not equal, so the rent is not either.

story.title: Ben and Ola
story.body:
Ben is 23 and works in a warehouse. Ola is 24 and teaches. Their rent is **$1,800**. Ben’s room is **200** square feet. Ola’s is **400**.

They split the rent by size: **$600** for Ben and **$1,200** for Ola. Electric is **$90** and internet is **$60**, and those they split in half.

They write a [[roommate agreement]] the same week they sign the [[lease]].

steps.prompt: What is Ben’s rent share on the 200-square-foot room?
What is Ola’s rent share on the 400-square-foot room?
Electric and internet are $150. Split in half, what does Ben add?
What does Ben pay in a normal month, rent share plus his half of the bills?
What does Ola pay in that same month?
steps.explain: $1,200 + $75 = $1,275. Together: $675 + $1,275 = $1,950, which is the $1,800 rent plus the $150 bills.

lessons.title: Moving Checklist
lessons.summary: Do them in an order that does not leave you paying two rents.

steps.title: Four beats
steps.body:
Notice, then the truck, then the utilities, then the photos and the keys.

Skipping the notice can cost a fee. Skipping the photos can cost the [[security deposit]].

steps.prompt: Put the move in order.
items: Book the truck and the helpers
Start the new utilities and stop the old ones
Photograph every room and return the keys
steps.explain: Notice protects you from a penalty. The truck and the power make the day work. The photos are the last word on the deposit.

steps.prompt: Why do the photos come after the place is empty?
choices: They show the condition you actually left
The landlord prefers a furnished photo
steps.explain: The deposit argument is about the day you hand over the keys.

steps.prompt: You should stop the old electric a month before you move out, to save money.
steps.explain: You still live there. Stop it the day you return the keys.

steps.prompt: The paper that tells the landlord you are leaving is written ___.

lessons.title: Sharpen Up
lessons.summary: Smart repetition on what you’re closest to forgetting.

lessons.title: Den Trial: Moving & Roommates
lessons.summary: 8 questions. Three strikes and you’re out.

steps.prompt: A move has a $200 truck, a $1,500 deposit, and $1,500 of first month’s rent. What is that trio?
One roommate moves out. The lease rent is $2,000. What can the landlord still require?
choices: Only the remaining roommate’s old half
Nothing until a new roommate signs
steps.explain: The lease amount stays until the lease changes.

steps.prompt: Rooms are 300 and 100 square feet. Rent is $2,000. What does the 300-square-foot room pay?
A roommate agreement replaces the lease.
steps.explain: It splits duties between roommates. The landlord still uses the lease.
